To catalyze, through regional and global level action, the improvement of conservation and effective governance of critical landscapes in the Congo Basin Forest Biome

Yes. We confirm that the child project design has considered socio-economic benefits to be delivered by the project as summarily presented below. These activities will be monitored and reported on during project implementation (at MTR and TER). The project will generate socio economic benefits for indigenous people, women and other minority groups through various planned activities. For example, the project will share knowledge and best practices with indigenous people and women from success models in the Congo basin and elsewhere in the use of innovative technologies in NTFP transformation and marketing. In collaboration with child projects, the regional project will support forest dependent communities in selected pilot landscapes to develop and adopt community life plans, supported by specific investment plans for key livelihood enhancing activities and forest commodities. As part of knowledge and experience sharing, the project will look at pilot and adapted models of conservation agreements for channeling multiple benefits to incentivize indigenous people, women and local communities for long term engagement in conservation initiatives. The project will conduct regional assessment of existing REDD+ projects and benefit sharing options to identify policy, institutional, legal and market constraints and propose adapted and appropriate gender responsive models and measures for use in regional dialogues and national benefit sharing processes. The project will gather information on success models, lessons learnt and best practices in sustainable forest-related value chains that can be used to empower local communities, forest dependent people, and partnering with the private sector.
